title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
claim: Many natural-language criteria are scored in parallel against one shared encoded context via a masked attention structure, yielding per-criterion verdicts.
layout: Single row, left-to-right; criteria sources, context, attention-mask grid, output record
description: A left-to-right flow diagram. At far left, three document icons (Regulation with scales, Deployer policy with shield, User instructions with person) merge via a bracket line into a stacked card labeled 'Natural Language Criteria' listing c1, c2, dots, cN. In the middle, a chat-style context x (alternating blue and gray bubbles) and a gray target text t bubble feed into the VFM. The VFM is drawn as a large grid with rows and columns x⊕t, c1, c2, ..., cN. Blue square blocks form a lower-triangular pattern on the x⊕t block and small triangles on the diagonal, and full blocks fill the column under x⊕t, which shows the tree-attention mask. A long arrow from the criteria stack enters the grid from below. At right, blue arrows lead to a boxed 'Compliance Record' showing per-criterion bar charts (blue, red, gray) with YES check, NO cross and N/A verdicts. The eye goes first to the blue attention-mask grid.
caption: Verifying Multiple Criteria with the VFM. Natural language criteria c1, . . . , cN from multiple sources are scored against the agent trace, consisting of context x and target text t. The VFM encodes the x ⊕t prefix once, and each criterion ci then branches independently under a tree-attention mask that isolates per-criterion attention while sharing the prefix’s KV cache. The output is a compliance record of softmax probabilities over ternary verdicts (YES / NO / N/A).
abstract: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable. We introduce the VFM, a tree-attention verifier that encodes the shared context and target text, and scores N natural language criteria in parallel, returning independent per-criterion ternary verdicts. The VFM is pretrained on CriteriaBank, a corpus of 394K (context, target, criterion, verdict) tuples spanning over 321K distinct criterion strings. A finetuned VFM-4B outperforms GPT-5.4 on a synthetic governance benchmark. On the DynaBench multi-criterion benchmark, it outperforms DynaGuard-4B on trace-level failure detection, and its per-criterion verdicts localize the violated rule and support focused escalation to a larger chain-of-thought judge. We show that CriteriaBank pretraining improves cross-domain transfer, particularly in the low-data regime, while matching a strong direct-finetuning control at full data. On a single H100, VFM-4B evaluates 1,000 criteria against a 4K-token context in under 2s at <11 GB VRAM, making it suitable for runtime verification.
